- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — dampen forecast slope downward for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0–0.3) and price is trending upward, model overestimates continuation — cap forecast growth at 2–3% above recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.3) and price is near support, model tends to underestimate — add 2–5% buffer to forecast if price has been below 30-day moving average.
- Model often underestimates downward moves in low-sentiment environments — if sentiment < -0.3 for 3+ consecutive days, add 3–5% downward bias to forecast.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to overconfidence in short-term momentum — if sentiment is volatile or mixed, reduce forecast variance by 15–20%.
- If true outcome deviates > 3% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent mean reversion — especially if sentiment is weak or neutral.
